catalog_quote: ６ アクセント 馬瀬(1961)などで指摘されているように，八丈方言では弁別的なアクセントを確認することはできない。調査データを見る限り，単独でのピッチパターンは第 1 モーラが高，第 2 モーラ以降が低となるものが多く見られた。 [NINJAL 1950, p. 176, §2 アクセント] 八丈島方言* のアクセントは、平山輝男氏の報告** にあるように、「アクセントなし」（いわゆる「一型アクセント」）である。 [Mase 1961, p. 43 fn. 1] ここで述べるのは狭義の音韻であり，音調については触れない．音調については平山輝男先生によりすでに 20 年前に一型音調であることが確認されている（「コトバ」第3巻第4号所収「言語島八丈島と黒潮」）．

new_statements.translation: 6 Accent. As pointed out by Mase (1961) and others, no distinctive accent can be identified in the Hachijō dialect. As far as the survey data show, the pitch pattern of words uttered in isolation was in most cases High on the first mora and Low from the second mora onward. [NINJAL 1950, p. 176:] The accent of the Hachijō-jima dialect is, as in Mr. Hirayama Teruo's report, 'no accent' (the so-called 'one-pattern accent'). [p. 177:] The result, as in Table 13, is that except for one person in K[ashitate], everyone lacks an accentual distinction between hashi 'bridge' and hashi 'chopsticks'.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Files checked under ( present and accurate). (1) = Matsuura Toshio 2013 「八丈方言の音韻」, NINJAL repository cover page confirms author 松浦年男, doi 10.15084/00002404, volume 『「消滅危機方言の調査・保存のための総合的研究」八丈方言調査報告書』 2013年10月. extracted text of p. 22 (printed p. 29) gives exactly: '６ アクセント 馬瀬(1961)などで指摘されているように，八丈方言では弁別的なアクセントを確認することはできない。調査データを見る限り，単独でのピッチパターンは第 1 モーラが高，第 2 モーラ以降が低となるものが多く見られた。' -- verbatim as quoted. The chapter's §1 states it is based on the Sept 2012 survey of the five Hachijō-jima villages (三根・大賀郷 = 坂下; 樫立・中之郷 = 坂上; 末吉), Aogashima excluded -- i.e. hach1239 proper. (2) = NINJAL 1950 『八丈島の言語調査』; the 300-dpi renders / printed pp. 176-177) read: '§2 アクセント 八丈島方言* のアクセントは、平山輝男氏の報告** にあるように、「ア…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Hachijō is an accentless (無アクセント / 一型) Japonic variety: there is no lexically distinctive word accent (no pitch accent contrasts of the Tokyo type, e.g. 橋 = 箸); phonetically, isolated words tend to be realized with a high first mora followed by low pitch, a non-contrastive default contour. No stress system is described.
new_statements.exceptions: NINJAL 1950 (p. 177, Table 13): 149 of 150 native residents across the five villages (Ōkagō, Mitsune, Kashitate, Nakanogō, Sueyoshi) showed no 橋/箸 distinction; the single exception (Kashitate, age 15) had an Aomori-born mother and had lived in Shizuoka. Matsuura notes the H-L.. isolation contour is a tendency ('多く見られた'), not categorical.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern lexical word accent (pitch), tested on citation forms / words in isolation (単独で); Matsuura's H on mora 1 then L is an isolation-form pitch contour, not a claimed phonological stress. Matsuura's data cover all five Hachijō-jima villages (Mitsune, Ōkagō, Kashitate, Nakanogō, Sueyoshi).
new_statements.identity_note: All three sources describe the Hachijō-jima dialects proper (five villages: Mitsune, Ōkagō = Sakashita; Kashitate, Nakanogō = Sakaue; Sueyoshi), i.e. glottocode hach1239; Mase 1961 centres on Nakanogō with notes on Mitsune, Kashitate and Utsuki (Hachijō-kojima). NINJAL 1950 pp. 178-179 additionally reports Aogashima and Hachijō-kojima as likewise 一型 (accentless). No separate glottocodes are involved.
